title: Project: The Shor Code Under Noise
summary: Build the nine-qubit Shor code, compute its logical failure probability under depolarizing noise exactly, and find the physical error rate below which encoding helps.
objectives: Implement and verify a Shor-code decoder against every single-qubit Pauli error
Compute the logical failure probability exactly by enumerating Pauli error patterns with their probabilities
Compare the encoded qubit with an unprotected qubit and locate the crossover p*
mission: Part 1: complete encode() and decode() as in lesson 4.4, so that qubit 0 returns to |ψ⟩ after an X, Y or Z error on any one of the nine qubits. Part 2: define logical_pauli(error), which takes a list of nine letters from I, X, Y, Z (error[q] acts on qubit q, applied between encoding and decoding) and returns the Pauli that is left on the logical qubit after majority-vote decoding. Part 3: define logical_failure(p), the probability that the logical Pauli is not I when every qubit independently suffers the depolarizing channel with probability p (I with probability 1 − p; X, Y, Z with probability p/3 each), and bare_failure(p) for one unprotected qubit. Part 4: store in p_star the smallest p > 0 at which logical_failure(p) = bare_failure(p), to within 0.003.

prediction.question: For small p, how does the logical failure probability of the Shor code scale?
options: Proportional to p, with a smaller coefficient than the bare qubit
Proportional to p², because the smallest failing pattern has two errors
Proportional to p³, because the code has distance 3
prediction.explanation: The code corrects every single-qubit error, so a failure needs at least two errors, and some pairs do fail: two X errors in one block leave a logical Z. The failure probability is therefore about N p² with N the number of failing pairs weighted by 1/9 (each of the two errors is an X or a Y with probability 2p/3), which beats the bare qubit only when p is small. The distance of the code is 3, but the Shor code does not correct every pair of errors, so the leading term is p², not p³.

hints: Encode and decode exactly as in lesson 4.4: the phase-flip code on the leaders 0, 3, 6, then a bit-flip code inside each block (0, 1, 2), (3, 4, 5), (6, 7, 8). Decode with CNOT, CNOT, Toffoli in each block, then Hadamard on the leaders and the same vote.

Work block by block. In a block, the inner vote flips the leader when at least two of the three qubits carry X or Y. The leader picks up a Z when an odd number of qubits carry Y or Z. Across blocks: the logical qubit gets an X when at least two blocks have an odd Z count, and a Z when an odd number of blocks had the inner vote fail. Both together make Y.

Each block has 4³ = 64 patterns, each with probability (1 − p)^(#I) (p/3)^(#X,Y,Z). Add these into four outcomes per block: (vote fails or not) × (Z parity odd or even). Combine three blocks (4³ = 64 combinations) and add the probability of every combination whose logical Pauli is not I. For p_star, evaluate logical_failure(p) − p on a grid or bisect: it is negative just above 0 and positive after the crossover.
